messages:
elena: Quick question — how should the rollout pin TTL interact with tombstones in the version graph? Saw a client route to a variant that had been tombstoned but still had a soft-expiry pin.

matt: Hmm. Is the tombstone applied at metadata-level (i.e. model node removed) or at routing time (flag that says DO_NOT_ROUTE)?

elena: Metadata-level. We write a tombstone record to the graph when a variant is deprecated, but the pin TTL cleanup job can lag. If a tenant has a pinned ref pointing to that variant, they keep getting routed.

jia: I think we need a stronger invariant: tombstone should imply immediate routing-invalidation, independent of pin TTL. Pins are for affinity, not for override of safety signals.

elena: Agree in principle. Concern: abrupt invalidation breaks canary rollouts where we pin test tenants to the old variant for safety. We need a way for a controlled downgrade vs a hard tombstone.

matt: Proposal: add a tombstone.type enum with values {SOFT, HARD}. SOFT marks deprecated but still routable for existing pinned leases; HARD forces immediate reject and returns a structured fallback.

jia: +1 for explicit types. Also add tombstone.meta.reason and tombstone.meta-actor so we can audit. And a tombstone.epoch that increments the model-version graph epoch to allow quick client probes to detect staleness.

elena: How would clients behave on HARD? Return 409? 412? Fallback to resolver? We need client-level guidance in spec.

sam: From an ops POV, HARD should trigger immediate fallback to the next compatible variant and emit a telemetry event. Client should get a stable error code so SDKs can surface a hint. I vote for 412 PRECONDITION_FAILED with body {"fallback":"variant-id","reason":"tombstone.hard"}.

matt: Sounds reasonable. For SOFT, client continues to route if its pin TTL still valid. But servers should start emitting deprecation headers to encourage migration. Also add a grace_window on the tombstone record: a wall-clock duration after which SERVICE will treat SOFT as HARD automatically.

jia: Implementation note: add tombstone.epoch and bump the global topology epoch when any HARD tombstone is written. Clients that cache routing decisions must compare cached_epoch < tombstone.epoch and then re-resolve. We already have epoch in placement but need to extend to rollout metadata.

elena: Good. Need to update the pin eviction job: it should ignore pins that reference HARD-tombstoned variants even if TTL unchanged. For SOFT, pin continues to be honored until pin.expiry or tombstone.grace_window elapses.

sam: Also add an admin workflow: soft->hard escalation requires a second confirmation flag. Avoid accidental mass-hard tombstones.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: NOTE: Created task #INF-9487 to add tombstone.type, epoch bump, and client error contract. Assigned to @matt. ETA: 2w.

matt: I'll open a formal spec PR today. Action items: 1) schema change for tombstone (type, epoch, grace_window, meta). 2) server routing change: treat HARD as immediate reject and emit fallback. 3) pin eviction change to ignore HARD refs. 4) SDK surface: map 412->fallback guidance + telemetry. 5) add unit + integration tests for epoch bumping and race scenarios.

elena: small nit: please also document race when pin updated concurrently with tombstone. Recommend server use compare-and-swap on pin.version vs tombstone.epoch to guarantee deterministic outcome.

elena: thanks all. If nobody objects I'll merge the proto changes into rollout-metadata v2 tomorrow. :thumbsup:

sam: No objections. Will prep a canary run plan for the rollout.

matt: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/rollout-metadata/pulls/142 — includes examples and a compatibility migration plan.

jia: I'll add evals to ensure no client-facing 5xx regressions.

elena: Great. Closing the thread — followups in PR comments.
